back: The ratio of the change in equilibrium national income to the initial change in autonomous spending (an injection).
k = 1 ÷ (MPS + MPT + MPM), all as fractions of national income.

front: Change in income from an injection?
What is the **marginal propensity to withdraw**?
back: The fraction of an extra dollar of income that leaks from the circular flow: MPS + MPT + MPM.
A higher MPS, MPT or MPM (larger leakages).

front: Name three limitations of the multiplier.
back: Time lags, limited spare capacity (inflation), crowding out and leakages/changing propensities.

front: Does the multiplier work for falls in injections?
back: Yes: a fall in investment, exports or government spending has a downward multiplier effect on income.
k = 1 ÷ (1 − MPC(1 − MRT) + MPM), with MPC out of disposable income.
